mathgap.title: Signed Equality for Difference Statements
mathgap.principle: When a statement equates two differences, treat both sides as signed equations preserving the order; do not take absolute values.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence of the form "The number of X that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of X that C and D have" appears.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "A has 5 more than B equals C has 5 more than D" as |A‑B| = |C‑D|, thereby losing the sign of each difference.

mathgap.title: Iterative Substitution and Propagation
mathgap.principle: Whenever a variable's value becomes known (through a direct count, a solved equation, or a transfer), substitute it into all pending equations and update dependent variables immediately.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After processing any statement that yields a concrete numeric value for a person.
mathgap.example: Failing to substitute a newly known count into later equations, leaving those equations unsolvable.

mathgap.title: Chronological Evaluation of Comparative Statements
mathgap.principle: Evaluate each comparative statement using the counts as they exist at that point in the text, after applying any earlier direct counts, transfers, or other updates.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When processing a comparative statement, use the current state of all counts, not the initial or final state.
mathgap.example: Using a person's final count to satisfy a comparative statement that appears earlier in the narrative.

mathgap.title: Query‑Focused Subsystem Extraction
mathgap.principle: Identify the minimal subset of equations and variables that are directly or indirectly connected to the queried person, ignoring unrelated statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Before solving the full system, trace dependencies from the query variable and prune irrelevant equations.
mathgap.example: Attempting to solve the entire large system, including many unrelated variables, which leads to unnecessary complexity and potential errors.

mathgap.title: Distinct Name Disambiguation
mathgap.principle: Treat each unique name as a separate variable, even if names differ by only a single character; avoid conflating similarly spelled names.
mathgap.when_to_apply: During parsing, map every distinct name token to its own variable before any reasoning.
mathgap.example: Mistaking "Le" and "Lee" for the same person and merging their counts, which corrupts the system of equations.

mathgap.title: Preserve Order in "Difference Between" Phrases
mathgap.principle: When a phrase says "the difference between the number of X that A and B have", interpret it as A − B, preserving the order named.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever the wording "difference between ... A and B" appears.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "difference between A and B" as B − A, thereby reversing the sign of the intended expression.

mathgap.title: General Comparative Interpretation (more/fewer)
mathgap.principle: Interpret "A has K more (fewer) items than B" as A − B = K (or = ‑K for fewer), preserving sign.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When parsing any comparative statement containing the words "more" or "fewer".
mathgap.example: Swapping the direction and writing B − A = K for "A has K more than B".

mathgap.title: Direct Count Handling with Overrides
mathgap.principle: When a statement says "X has N items", set X's count to N at that point, overriding any previous value (including those from earlier transfers or derived counts).
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a direct count statement is encountered in the narrative.
mathgap.example: Ignoring a later "X has N" and keeping the earlier count, resulting in an inconsistent total.

mathgap.title: Chronological Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: Apply each transfer statement in the order given, subtracting the specified amount from the giver and adding it to the receiver at that moment.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When processing a sentence of the form "X gives K items to Y".
mathgap.example: Applying transfers out of order, causing the giver's count to be wrong for a later comparative statement that depends on it.

mathgap.description: Swapped direction in 'has K more than' statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model confuses the order of subtraction in comparative statements, treating "A has K more than B" as B − A = K.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Remember that "A has K more than B" translates to A − B = K (and "fewer" to A − B = ‑K).

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes differences are always non‑negative and drops the sign when converting "difference between A and B".
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve the sign and order: interpret "difference between A and B" as A − B, not |A − B|.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the chronological order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats transfers as commutative or applies them after all other statements, losing the intermediate state needed for later comparisons.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process each transfer in the exact order it appears, updating counts before evaluating any subsequent statement.

mathgap.description: Treating 'has N' as an initial count regardless of position
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes a direct count sets a permanent initial value and never updates it, even when later statements override it.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply direct count statements as overrides at the point they appear, replacing any prior value for that person.
